t: For necessary expenses for alteration or removal of obstructive bridges, $16,000,000, to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation of funds for the alteration or removal of obstructive bridges. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting contrary reading, since the text only makes money available.
fable.s: For necessary expenses for alteration or removal of obstructive bridges, $16,000,000, to remain available until expended.

opus.w: This section only sets aside $16,000,000 to alter or remove obstructive bridges. It does not require or invite consultation, comment, hearings, advisory input, or lawsuits by anyone outside the federal government. Bridge owners may be affected, but the text gives them no role in any federal decision, so it is not participation.
opus.s: For necessary expenses for alteration or removal of obstructive bridges, $16,000,000, to remain available until expended.
opus.b:
Step 1: The one tempting reading is that removing obstructive bridges could involve bridge owners or local governments. That fails because the text says nothing about any outside party taking part in a federal decision. It only provides money.

Step 2: The section is just an appropriation of money. It has no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing funds for the alteration or removal of obstructive bridges. It does not mention any requirement for consultation, public comment, hearings, or coordination with outside parties (such as bridge owners, local governments, or the public) before the federal government makes a decision or takes action. The determination of which bridges are obstructive is an internal administrative matter not described here as involving outside participation.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses for alteration or removal of obstructive bridges, $16,000,000, to remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "obstructive bridges" implies a decision-making process involving bridge owners or local governments to determine which bridges are obstructive, thus implying participation. However, the text itself is merely an appropriation clause authorizing funds for a specific purpose. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or coordination with outside parties. The determination of which bridges are obstructive is likely an internal administrative or engineering decision by the federal agency (e.g., Army Corps of Engineers), not a participatory process defined in this section.
